q-73923.name: Question 1
q-73923.worked_solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $m$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5{a}_{1}+m{a}_{2} & =0 \\ 5[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+m[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ m[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ m[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-30 \\ 10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the first components, we get 

$$
-5m=-30\,⟹\,m=6.
$$

But then

$$
\begin{aligned}6[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-30 \\ 18\end{aligned}]\ne [\begin{aligned}-30 \\ 10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, there is no $m$ such that $5{a}_{1}+m{a}_{2}=0.$

EXPLANATION

Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the m term, we get

5a1+ma2=05[6−2]+m[−53]=[00]m[−53]=[00]−5[6−2]m[−53]=[−3010].

Equating the first components, we get

−5m=−30⟹m=6.

q-34602.name: Question 2
q-34602.worked_solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $k$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8{a}_{1}+k{a}_{2} & =0 \\ 8[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 6 \\ -4\end{aligned}]+k[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ k[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-8[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 6 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ k[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}24 \\ -48 \\ 32\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the first components, we get 

$$
-2k=24\,⟹\,k=-12.
$$

But then 

$$
\begin{aligned}-12[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}24 \\ -36 \\ 48\end{aligned}]\ne [\begin{aligned}24 \\ -48 \\ 32\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, there is no $k$ such that 
 $8{a}_{1}+k{a}_{2}=0.$

q-105161.name: Question 3
q-105161.problem:
Find the value of ${x}_{1}-{x}_{2}$ given that $7a+4x=b$ and

$$
a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4 \\ -3 \\ -6\end{aligned}].
$$
q-105161.worked_solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}7a+4x & =b \\ 4x & =b-7a \\ x & =\frac{1}{4}(b-7a) \\ x & =\frac{1}{4}([\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4 \\ -3 \\ -6\end{aligned}]-7[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]) \\ x & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 4 \\ 4 \\ -20\end{aligned}] \\ x & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=-2-1=-3.$

Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate x, we get

7a+4x=b4x=b−7ax=14(b−7a)x=14([−14−3−6]−7[10−12])x=14[−844−20]x=[−211−5].

q-105159.name: Question 4
q-105159.worked_solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4a+3x & =b \\ 3x & =b-4a \\ x & =\frac{1}{3}(b-4a) \\ x & =\frac{1}{3}([\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ -4\end{aligned}]) \\ x & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 6 \\ 15\end{aligned}] \\ x & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-34054.name: Question 5
q-34054.problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
q-34054.worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=5 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=3 \\ {x}_{2}=2\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation we get ${x}_{2}=2$, which we substitute into the second equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} & =3 \\ -{x}_{1}+2 & =3 \\ {x}_{1} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=2$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & =5 \\ -(-1)+2(2) & =5 \\ 5 & =5,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=2,$ which means

$$
-{a}_{1}+2{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-1+2=1.
$$

x1[−1−10]+x2[211]=[532][−x1−x10]+[2x2x2x2]=[532][−x1+2x2−x1+x2x2]=[532].

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

q-105167.name: Question 6
q-105167.problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
q-105167.worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1} \\ -3{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-7{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2}=-9 \\ -3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=3 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the first and the second equations we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} & =-6 \\ {x}_{2} & =3,\end{aligned}
$$

which we substitute into the second equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=3 \\ -3{x}_{1}+5(3) & =3 \\ -3{x}_{1} & =-12 \\ {x}_{1} & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=4$ and ${x}_{2}=3$ into the third equation and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=1 \\ (4)-(3) & =1 \\ 1 & =1,\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement. 

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=4$ and ${x}_{2}=3,$ which means

$$
4{a}_{1}+3{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=4+3=7.
$$

Question 6
?

Consider the vectors

a1=[3−31],a2=[−75−1],b=[−931].

If x1a1+x2a2=b, then what is x1+x2?

a
4
b
6
c
5
d
3
e
7

Correct
EXPLANATION

If x1a1+x2a2=b, then we have

x1[3−31]+x2[−75−1]=[−931][3x1−3x1x1]+[−7x25x2−x2]=[−931][3x1−7x2−3x1+5x2x1−x2]=[−931].

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

{3x1−7x2=−9−3x1+5x2=3x1−x2=1

Adding the first and the second equations we get −2x2=−6x2=3, which we substitute into the second equation to get

−3x1+5x2=3−3x1+5(3)=3−3x1=−12x1=4.

Finally, we substitute x1=4 and x2=3 into the third equation and obtain

x1−x2=1(4)−(3)=11=1, which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is x1=4 and x2=3, which means

4a1+3a2=b.

Consequently,

x1+x2=4+3=7.

q-74035.name: Question 7
q-74035.problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
q-74035.worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ 3{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {x}_{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} \\ 3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4 \\ -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=-3 \\ 5{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=4 \\ 3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-4\end{aligned}
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 2 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}]
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 2 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0.2 & 0.8 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=-{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0.2 & 0.8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=-3 \\ {x}_{2}+\,0.2{x}_{3}=0.8 \\ {x}_{3}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-1.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get 

$$
{x}_{2}+0.2(-1)=0.8\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=1.
$$

   

Finally,  substituting ${x}_{2}=1$ into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-(1)=-3\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-2.
$$

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-2$, ${x}_{2}=1$, and ${x}_{3}=-1,$ which means  

$$
-2{a}_{1}+{a}_{2}-{a}_{3}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-2+1-1=-2.
$$

q-105169.problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 6 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -8 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
q-105169.worked_solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 6 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -8 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 5{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ 6{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{3} \\ -8{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} \\ 5{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}-8{x}_{3} \\ -2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=2 \\ 5{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}-8{x}_{3}=-3 \\ -2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=4\end{aligned}
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 5 & 6 & -8 & -3 \\ -2 & -2 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 5 & 6 & -8 & -3 \\ -2 & -2 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -13 \\ -2 & -2 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -13 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=2 \\ {x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=-13 \\ 0=8.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0=8$  gives a false statement. So the system has no solution.
